title: Check: Reactions of Metals with Water and Acids (2)

questions.stem: What are the products when a metal reacts with water?
questions.explanation: When a metal reacts with water, the products are a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas. The general equation is: Metal + Water → Metal hydroxide + Hydrogen. For example, 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂.

questions.stem: Why does copper not react with dilute hydrochloric acid?

options.text: Copper is above hydrogen in the reactivity series
Copper only reacts with concentrated acids
Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series and cannot displace it
Copper reacts too slowly to observe

questions.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, meaning it is less reactive than hydrogen. Because of this, copper cannot displace hydrogen from the acid, so no reaction occurs with dilute hydrochloric acid or dilute sulfuric acid.
